Echoes Of Killarney / Is Leir Dom Intinn Cheataí / Mo Shéamuisín (Amaj)

Here’s Séamus Begley’s version of this slide with a bit of divilish variation at the end that he and Méabh would sometimes play. Seamus liked to first play this tune in G major and then transpose it to A major. He often did it with other G major tunes as well. Combined with his favourite grey Paolo Soprani in Eb and a very high pace, this propelled the tunes to the stratosphere, far above the noise of the pub. This also made playing on the fiddle a bit precarious since you tuned it half step up and the tension of the E string was ferocious while the bow hand had to push harder than ever to keep up with the sheer volume of the session… “I like this key, it makes fiddlers work harder!” Séamus once told me after finishing up a set of slides :-D

Máire and Séamus Ó Beaglaoich titled this tune Is Leir Dom Intinn Cheataí on Plancstaí Bhaile na bPoc while Méabh Ní Bheaglaoich called it Mo Shéamuisín on Cuisle.

↳ Posted by Bregolas on February 24th, 2024.

Echoes Of Killarney, X:11 / Art O’Keeffe’s No. 2 / Denis McMahon’s Slide (S: Denis Murphy & Art O’Keeffe)

Denis Murphy’s version of this slide from the Breandán Breathnach recordings (1966). This is one of the tunes Murphy’s neighbour Art O’Keeffe liked to play and Denis might’ve learned it from him. The version from this particular take is close to that of Art O’Keeffe’s who played it in a set with this another, much lesser-known tune: https://thesession.org/tunes/24607

↳ Posted by Bregolas on January 2nd, 2025.

The original link is thesession.org/tunes/5945
